## Design

### 2026-10-19 – I wrote a test program based off of some sound samples I found online of the base string non tampered with. I then took these samples and wrote a python program that modifies them using scipy then sav

**4h**

I wrote a test program based off of some sound samples I found online of the base string non tampered with. I then took these samples and wrote a python program that modifies them using scipy then saves the modified sound files, the sound files are on github if you want to hear them, theres certainly some room for improvement, but I think this idea can work.

### 2026-10-24 – I routed the pcb, this was very challenging as I inadvertantly routed the schematic in such a way that caused a lot of crossing back and forth, I was able to figure it out in the end however. This pro

**6h**

I routed the pcb, this was very challenging as I inadvertantly routed the schematic in such a way that caused a lot of crossing back and forth, I was able to figure it out in the end however. This process connected everything together and laid the framework for the digital pedal steel guitar, I opted to give the power delivery lines as well as ground their own separate layers, this gave me a lot more room to work with.

### 2026-10-25 – I wrote the code that will handle the changing simulation, this code takes in the raw sound from the piezo sensors and then modifies the pitch to make it sound as if you had pressed the actual mechani

**8h**

I wrote the code that will handle the changing simulation, this code takes in the raw sound from the piezo sensors and then modifies the pitch to make it sound as if you had pressed the actual mechanical changing pedal or knee lever on a pedal steel guitar
